Which one is best depends on how much power you need. I read OutdoorGearLab's tested picks and a page on the BLUETTI AC180. Wired's page wouldn't load, so I couldn't use it.

**Top picks for camping**

| Need | Pick | Capacity | Weight | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Best all-around for most campers | [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) | 1,152 Wh | about 35 lbs (16 kg) | $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF |
| Best value and lighter weight | Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 | 1,024 Wh (890 Wh measured usable) | 25.2 lbs | $799 list; OutdoorGearLab says it was under $530 on sale |
| Best for long off-grid trips | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042 Wh (1,710 Wh measured usable) | 38.9 lbs | $1,499 list; OutdoorGearLab says it was under $900 on sale |
| Best for phones, laptops and lights | Jackery Explorer 300 | 293 Wh (260 Wh measured usable) | 7.1 lbs | $289 |
| Cheapest and smallest | Anker Solix 521 | 256 Wh (192 Wh measured usable) | 8.4 lbs | $230 |

I only have a purchase link for the BLUETTI. For the others, search the product name on Amazon or the maker's site.

**Why the BLUETTI AC180 is my default pick**
- It has a 1,800 W AC output, so it can run a small electric cooler, a CPAP, or a kettle.
- Its LiFePO4 battery is rated for 3,500+ cycles.
- It takes up to 500 W of solar input.
- It recharges from the wall to 80% in about 45 minutes in Turbo mode.
- It has a 5-year warranty.
- It has no expansion port, so you can't add extra battery capacity later.
- The $474.05 price is for the station only. A $599 bundle adds a 100 W solar panel.
- The code was tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-21. Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through its link, at no cost to you, and you should confirm the final price at checkout.

**How to choose**
- **Weekend car camping with phones, lights and a laptop:** the Jackery Explorer 300 is enough, and it's easy to carry.
- **Running a fridge, CPAP or small appliances:** go with the BLUETTI AC180 or the Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2. The Anker is about 10 lbs lighter and charges very fast (about 56 minutes), but OutdoorGearLab notes it has a loud fan.
- **Several days off-grid:** the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 has the most runtime of these. It is heavy and can't be expanded.

Check current prices before buying. The "sale" prices above came from OutdoorGearLab's page and may have changed.

Sources: [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station), [Dealectric BLUETTI AC180 page](https://dealectric.com/lab/V8/bluetti-ac180)
